name: Tarrytown
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Tarrytown, NY 2026
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Tarrytown and Sleepy Hollow, NY for 2026: free trolley Winter Stroll, Dickens's Christmas Carol and Christmas at Sunnyside.
lede: Tarrytown and Sleepy Hollow share one holiday weekend, with a free trolley stroll, a Dickens play in a historic church and Christmas at Washington Irving's Sunnyside.
celebrates: The two Hudson River villages celebrate together. The Sleepy Hollow Tarrytown Chamber of Commerce holds its 6th annual Winter Stroll on Saturday, December 12, with free jolly trolleys looping between both villages, a craft pop-up, food trucks and a Sleepy Hollow tree lighting at 5 pm. Historic Hudson Valley adds Dickens's Christmas Carol at the Old Dutch Church and Christmas at Washington Irving's Sunnyside, where families can make a holiday craft, hear seasonal stories and visit with Saint Nicholas. Shops on Main Street in Tarrytown and Beekman Avenue in Sleepy Hollow stay open late with treats and discounts.
lastyear: We did not find a published 2025 recap of the Winter Stroll, so this page leans on the host pages for 2026. The chamber calls this year's stroll its 6th annual, which means the tradition began in 2021 and has grown to two villages, two free trolleys and a long list of participating shops. Historic Hudson Valley also runs its holiday program in Sleepy Hollow Country each season, with historic site tours at Philipsburg Manor on weekends and a Holiday Boutique that opens alongside the other events.
facts: Christmas at Sunnyside takes place at the home of Washington Irving, the author of The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, and Historic Hudson Valley still operates the house as a museum. The Dickens play is staged in the Old Dutch Church of Sleepy Hollow, and the organization says it offers performances at 2, 3:30 and 5 pm on its weekend dates. The chamber's Winter Stroll also invites families to vote for a favorite festive storefront decoration and to enter an ugly sweater contest.
trains: We did not find a Christmas train ride in Tarrytown or Sleepy Hollow itself. Our New York guide at /blog/christmas-train-ride-new-york lists the Christmas train rides across the state, including the Long Island and Hudson Valley rides. Tarrytown has a Metro-North Hudson Line station, so families coming from New York City can take the train up the river and walk to Main Street for the Winter Stroll. The free jolly trolleys then carry riders between Tarrytown Music Hall and Sleepy Hollow.
traditions: The chamber's 6th annual stroll puts free jolly trolleys, a craft pop-up and shop treats in both villages on December 12.
A Salvation Army choir performs at the 5 pm tree lighting in Robertson Park during the stroll.
Historic Hudson Valley stages the Dickens story in the Old Dutch Church on weekends from December 12 to 20.
Washington Irving's home opens for crafts, stories and Saint Nicholas on December 19 and 20.
Families vote for a favorite decorated storefront during the Winter Stroll.
kidfact: Washington Irving, who wrote The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, lived at Sunnyside, and each December the house opens for holiday crafts and stories.
faq: What are the best Christmas events for kids in Tarrytown and Sleepy Hollow?

The Winter Stroll on December 12 has free trolleys, a craft pop-up and a tree lighting. Historic Hudson Valley adds Dickens's Christmas Carol at the Old Dutch Church and Christmas at Sunnyside with crafts, stories and Saint Nicholas, which suits all ages.
Is the Tarrytown and Sleepy Hollow Winter Stroll free?

The chamber says the jolly trolleys are free and lists no single admission price for the stroll. Individual shops, workshops and food set their own prices, so plan on paying for treats and activities you choose.
Where can kids meet Santa in Sleepy Hollow?

During the Winter Stroll on December 12, Santa and other characters visit Los Andes Bakery at 180 Valley Street from 2 to 4 pm for photos, cocoa and other surprises, according to the chamber's schedule.
Is Dickens's Christmas Carol good for young children?
Historic Hudson Valley recommends the show for ages 10 and up, with children's tickets at $42. Younger kids may do better at Christmas at Sunnyside, which the organization recommends for all ages.
Do I need tickets for Christmas at Sunnyside?
Yes. Historic Hudson Valley says advance tickets are required and lists them at $30. Buy them on the organization's ticket site, where the December 19 and 20 dates are posted.
